about: The captain across the saga: two meetings with an older captain (from Cargo 2 at an outpost, from Cargo 3 at the portal) and the clone. Without an imported record the older captain is never named. With one, the scene uses the record's name: the captain's own name means the same person grown old; another name is the captain the player went on to play in that part, who knew this one. Intros: a fresh captain starts with a loan and a docking slot; a captain carried in from another playthrough or a later part arrives with a short account of who they were and why they start again.

clone.about: grown by a research colony's insurer from the captain's customs scan; same face, same licence, same debts

met_the_stranger.about: the captain spoke with the old hauler at an outpost bar

kept_the_pellet.about: the captain kept the pellet the old hauler paid with: a Hansa Mark, before there were any

heard_the_warning.about: the captain listened to the older captain at the portal

closed_the_channel.about: the captain cut the older captain off at the portal

scanned_at_customs.about: the captain's customs scan is on file with a research colony's insurer

clone_partner.about: the captain and the clone split the routes

clone_reported.about: the captain reported the clone to the insurer

clone_fight.about: the captain went after the clone

clone_let_go.about: the captain beat the clone in a fight and let it run

vertex_array_kren.about: the captain measured the grey alloy samples before the fire and gave {ancient_scholar.short} the cartridge (an errand from 2533)

intro.fresh.title: Docking slot 14
text: Every hauler starts the same way: a loan, a ship older than the loan officer, and a docking slot at {place} paid up until Friday.
The dock master spells your name wrong on the slot. It will be a few years before anyone corrects it.

intro.again.title: Again
text: {origin.name} walked away from a career as {origin.rank} before it was finished, and found that walking away is not a trade.
The bank, which remembers everybody, lends you one ship and a loan with your old account number on it.
After the founding of the Hansa, {origin.name} retired to a farm drum at Barnard's Star and lasted eleven months.
You sell the drum, buy one tired hauler and sign the same loan papers as the first time, out of superstition.
The First Legion gave {origin.name} a pension, a medal and a desk. The desk did not survive.
You resign your commission on a Tuesday and buy a hauler on the Wednesday. It has no guns. That is the point.
{origin.name} filed the course home and waited for someone to read it. Nobody did.
If the scholars will not fly it, a hauler might. Haulers need routes, money and a ship. You start with the ship.
Retirement on the most expensive drum at Barnard's Star turned out to be one long complaint about prices.
{origin.name} sells everything and starts again with one ship, to find out whether it was luck.

intro.from_cargo2.title: Forty years early
text: The last thing {origin.name}, {origin.rank}, remembers is a ring segment turning the wrong way. The first thing is this dock, forty years before your own career began.
You have a ship nobody else wanted, a rank on a card no clerk here can read, and {origin.turns} turns of experience that have not happened yet.
You kept one thing from your own time: the navigation computer, pulled from your old ship before you sold it.

intro.errand.title: An errand, early
text: {origin.name} went into a needle in 2533 and came out a hundred and thirteen years early, with a promise to keep.

On level nine at Gamma, a plaque will one day carry twelve names and a blank thirteenth line 'for the hauler who brought the air'. The miners are not trapped yet. Your rank has not been invented. Your hands still know how to fly.
{origin.name} went into a needle in 2533 and came out a hundred and thirteen years early, with two promises to keep.

A blank thirteenth line on a plaque at Gamma, 'for the hauler who brought the air'. A gap in {ancient_scholar}'s notes where the shape of the grey alloy should be, before a fire takes the samples. Neither has happened yet. Your rank has not been invented. Your hands still know how to fly.
{origin.name} went into a needle in 2533 and came out a hundred and thirteen years early, with a promise to keep.

One day {ancient_scholar} will have three shards of grey alloy on a bench at the Stellar Institute, and a fire will take them. In 2533 her notes have a gap where their shape should be. Measure them first. Your rank has not been invented. Your hands still know how to fly.

intro.from_cargo3.title: Further back than anyone
text: {origin.name}, {origin.rank}, was standing at the restart of the Gyrotron, more than a century from now, when it turned once in the wrong direction.
Here the Hansa does not exist, the Mandate is three security firms, and your rank has not been invented. Your hands still know how to fly. That will have to do.
In your pocket: a shard of grey alloy, still warm.

trail.vertex.title: Before the fire
text: {ancient_scholar.short} has the three samples on a bench at the Stellar Institute: comet ice from Scholz's Star, collision dust from Fomalhaut, Gamma's tailings. You know what she does not. Soon the store will burn, and every sample with it.

You borrow the Institute's scanner for a night and measure the three shards into one shape, the shape the segment had before anyone cut it: its raw coordinates, a Vertex Array, on a data cartridge. 'Why would I need a copy?' she asks. You do not answer.
She tapes the cartridge into her notebook anyway and asks you to write the label. You write: 'The shape, measured before the fire. For T.K.'

self.outpost.title: The old hauler
self.outpost.text: In the station bar an old hauler pays for your drink before you have ordered it. The hauler taps the glass twice before drinking, the way you do, and asks after your ship by its real name, the one you have never painted on the hull.

variants.text: In the station bar an old hauler pays for your drink before you have ordered it. The name tag says {visitor.name}. That is your name. The face above it is yours too, with forty more years on it, and it would rather not discuss that.

In the station bar an old hauler pays for your drink before you have ordered it. The name tag says {visitor.name}, {visitor.rank}. You have never met. The hauler talks to you like an old crewmate who owes you money.

choices.say: Ask how they know the ship

notes: outposts and research colonies: explorers rarely stop at outposts

self.outpost.advice.title: Paid in advance
text: 'One day you will sell her at Epsilon for less than she is worth,' the old hauler says. 'Pull the navigation computer before you do.'

Then the hauler leaves. The bartender shows you how the round was paid: a small, heavy pellet stamped with a number. Nobody at the bar knows what it is. You recognise the number. It is your ship's registry.

choices.say: Buy the pellet from the bartender

self.portal.title: The ship on the far side
self.portal.text: A ship is waiting on the far side of the ring. It is your hull, older, patched where yours has not been hit yet. Its captain opens a voice channel with no picture. The voice is yours, worn down. 'When they restart it,' it says, 'make sure it starts from home.'

variants.text: A ship is waiting on the far side of the ring. {visitor.name}, {visitor.rank}, opens a channel, picture and all. It is your face with a scar you have not earned yet. 'When they restart it,' the older you says, 'make sure it starts from home.'

A ship is waiting on the far side of the ring. {visitor.name}, {visitor.rank}, opens a channel. You have never seen this captain. The captain says your name the way people read names off a memorial, then: 'When they restart it, make sure it starts from home.'

clone.scan.title: Customs scan
clone.scan.text: Customs at the research colony scans every visitor down to the cell. The form says the scan is for insurance. The small print says the colony's insurer may grow a replacement crew from it if yours is lost. You sign. The alternative is not docking.

clone.bill.title: A bill from Gamma
clone.bill.text: A repair yard at Gamma sends you a bill for work on your ship. Your ship has never been to that yard. The work order is signed with your thumbprint, and the yard notes that you tipped well.

clone.meet.title: {clone}
text: Two berths down sits a ship of your class with your registry, one digit off.
Its captain has your face, your licence and, under the insurer's contract, your debts. The clone has paid off more of them than you have.

rogue_captain.1.title: {clone}: the fight
rogue_captain.1.text: The clone flies the way you fly. That is the problem.
notes: was: an unused chain with no trigger; now the clone's fight (stage data: enemy_stats)

rogue_captain.2.title: {clone}: after
rogue_captain.2.text: The other ship breaks off and runs. You know the course it will take, because it is the course you would take. You let it go.

text: A fire in the sample store of the Stellar Institute at TRAPPIST-1. Nobody hurt. Every sample of the grey alloy is gone, with the notes, and the fire door was propped open with a chair from somebody else's lab.
{ancient_scholar.short} sits on the steps with a smoke-black notebook. 'Somebody does not want this to be true,' she says. 'Or wants it to be true only for them.'
The chair comes from a security liaison's office that rents a room at the Institute and has never been seen to use it. The name on the door is {serac.short}.
You came back a hundred and thirteen years to measure the samples, and the fire was faster. The errand stays in your record; another line of time may be luckier.

notes: amended: a captain on the errand from 2533 learns it came too late (the errand stays open)
